prompt: What is the difference between quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC)?
correct: QA is the plan and process; QC is inspecting and testing the actual work
options: QA is the plan and process; QC is inspecting and testing the actual work
QA is done by the owner; QC is done only by the general contractor
QA is inspecting the finished work; QC is writing the quality plan
They mean the same thing and are used interchangeably
explanation: QA sets up the plan, procedures and audits that give confidence the work will meet requirements; QC checks the actual installed work against those requirements.

prompt: On an Inspection and Test Plan, what is the difference between a hold point and a witness point?
correct: Hold: work stops until signed off. Witness: the party is invited to watch, and work may go on if they don't come
options: Hold: work stops until signed off. Witness: the party is invited to watch, and work may go on if they don't come
Hold: the party is invited to watch. Witness: work stops until signed off
Both stop the work until the owner signs
Neither stops the work; both are only notifications
explanation: A hold point is a mandatory stop: the next step cannot start until the named party has inspected and signed. A witness point only requires notice; work can proceed if the witness does not attend.

prompt: A cable reel arrives gouged and with no lot number on it. What do you do?
correct: Tag it HOLD, photograph it, log it, tell your supervisor, raise an NCR; don't install it
options: Tag it HOLD, photograph it, log it, tell your supervisor, raise an NCR; don't install it
Install it if the crew is waiting, and write the lot number in later
Send it straight back to the supplier without recording anything
Cut off the damaged outer layers and install the rest
explanation: Receiving inspection exists to stop non-conforming material before it is built in: segregate it, document it with photos, report it and let the NCR process decide its disposition.

prompt: When do you write an RFI (Request for Information)?
correct: When drawings or specs are unclear or conflict and it affects the work
options: When drawings or specs are unclear or conflict and it affects the work
Every morning, to report the crew count
Only after the work has been installed and failed inspection
When you want to change a supplier's price
explanation: Ask in writing, never guess: an RFI gets a documented answer from the designer before the work is built.

prompt: What are the steps to close a non-conformance report (NCR)?
correct: Identify, document, contain, disposition, fix, re-inspect, close with evidence
options: Identify, document, contain, disposition, fix, re-inspect, close with evidence
Identify, fix, close; photos are optional
Raise it, wait for the owner to close it, then fix the work
Document it and close it at the end of the project
explanation: An NCR is only closed when the fix has been re-inspected and the closure evidence (photos, test results, signatures) is attached.

prompt: Point-to-point checkout (each field device to controller to the displayed value or alarm) happens at which commissioning level?
correct: L3, start-up / pre-functional
options: L3, start-up / pre-functional
L1, factory witness testing
L5, integrated systems testing
L4, functional performance testing
explanation: At Level 3 each piece of equipment is started on its own and the commissioning team verifies controls point by point.
quote: the commissioning team verifies controls point by point, confirming that each sensor reads correctly and each command moves the right device

prompt: In the five-level commissioning scheme, what is verified at Level 2 (delivery and installation verification)?
correct: Equipment arrives undamaged and is installed correctly
options: Equipment arrives undamaged and is installed correctly
Major equipment meets specification before shipping
Each system performs all its functions at design load
All systems work together through real failure scenarios
explanation: Level 2 covers receiving inspection, pre-functional checklists, torque checks and labeling.
quote: Delivery and installation verification Equipment arrives undamaged and is installed correctly

prompt: Commissioning Level 1 is ____: major equipment is proven to meet specification before it ships.
correct: factory witness testing
options: factory witness testing
integrated systems testing
functional performance testing
start-up and component testing
explanation: Problems are cheaper and quicker to fix at the factory than on site.
quote: L1 Factory witness testing Major equipment meets specification before shipping

prompt: Which commissioning level puts all systems together through real failure scenarios, such as a utility failure with generator start?
correct: Level 5, integrated systems testing
options: Level 5, integrated systems testing
Level 2, delivery and installation verification
Level 3, start-up and component testing
Level 1, factory witness testing
explanation: Integrated systems testing is the culmination of commissioning.
quote: L5 Integrated systems testing All systems work together through real failure scenarios

prompt: At which commissioning level are vendor start-up, NETA acceptance tests and insulation resistance tests done?
correct: Level 3, start-up and component testing
options: Level 3, start-up and component testing
Level 1, factory witness testing
Level 5, integrated systems testing
Level 2, delivery and installation verification
explanation: Level 3 brings each piece of equipment to life on its own.
quote: L3 Start-up and component testing Each piece of equipment starts and operates on its own Vendor start-up, NETA acceptance tests, insulation resistance, relay settings

prompt: Why can a system not start functional performance testing while its components have not passed start-up?
correct: Each commissioning level is a gate for the next
options: Each commissioning level is a gate for the next
Functional tests are only ever done at the factory
Start-up is optional when a vendor is on site
Functional tests are sampled, so the order does not matter
explanation: Sequencing the levels means each one tests something new instead of rediscovering problems a lower level should have caught.
quote: Each level is a gate. Equipment that fails factory testing is not shipped

prompt: During a scripted commissioning test, a step produces an unexpected result. What should happen?
correct: Stop, record it in the issues log, and resume only after the cause is understood
options: Stop, record it in the issues log, and resume only after the cause is understood
Improvise a workaround so the test can finish today
Skip the step and mark it as passed
Repeat the step until it passes
explanation: Deviations from the script are never improvised during a live test.
quote: Stop, record it in the issues log, and resume only after the cause is understood.

prompt: Which items does a Level 2 pre-functional check look at?
correct: Anchorage, clearances, terminations, torque, grounding and labeling
options: Anchorage, clearances, terminations, torque, grounding and labeling
Only the paint finish and the nameplate
Full-load failure testing with a load bank
Factory test reports only, nothing on site
explanation: Many problems that would surface in functional testing, such as a missing ground conductor, are caught at Level 2.
quote: Delivery condition and correct installation: anchorage, clearances, terminations, torque, grounding, labeling.

prompt: Why are installation checks usually done on every unit even when functional tests are only sampled?
correct: Random installation defects such as a loose connection are easily missed by sampling
options: Random installation defects such as a loose connection are easily missed by sampling
Sampling is not allowed by any standard
Installation checks are cheaper than paperwork
Every unit always has a firmware error
explanation: Sampling works for systematic defects (a wrong firmware version on every unit) but poorly for random ones.
quote: Random defects are easily missed by sampling; inspect all units and sample only systematic risks.

prompt: In commissioning, a ____ is the documentation handed to operations for a system.
correct: turnover package
options: turnover package
punch list
test script
sequence of operation
explanation: Turnover packages gather test records, the issues log, as-builts, settings, manuals and training records.
quote: Turnover package The documentation handed to operations for a system.

prompt: What are acceptance criteria in a test script?
correct: Measurable limits a test result must meet
options: Measurable limits a test result must meet
The names of the people who witness the test
The steps that return the system to normal
The list of instruments used
explanation: Acceptance is judged against numbers, not impressions.
quote: Acceptance criteria Measurable limits a test result must meet.

prompt: What is a pre-functional checklist?
correct: A list verifying that equipment is installed correctly before start-up
options: A list verifying that equipment is installed correctly before start-up
A test of all systems together through failure scenarios
The owner's list of unpaid invoices
A list of defects found after handover
explanation: Pre-functional checklists belong to Level 2 commissioning.
quote: Pre-functional checklist A list verifying that equipment is installed correctly before start-up.

prompt: What should be in hand before a facility accepts handover of a system?
correct: Test records, as-builts, settings, manuals and training
options: Test records, as-builts, settings, manuals and training
Only the final invoice
Only a verbal confirmation from the installer
Nothing: documents can follow a year later
explanation: Incomplete documentation is one of the most common complaints of operators taking over new facilities.
quote: Require test records, as-builts, settings, manuals and training first.

prompt: Besides tracking day-to-day jobsite activity, why do daily logs matter?
correct: They are records in case of financial or legal disputes
options: They are records in case of financial or legal disputes
They replace the need for RFIs
They are only used to order lunch for the crew
They are destroyed at the end of each week
explanation: Entries should be accurate and objective so they hold up later.
quote: as invaluable records in case of financial or legal disputes

prompt: Daily log entries should serve as accurate, ____ records of weather, subcontractors and equipment on site.
correct: objective
options: objective
optional
verbal
estimated
explanation: Write what happened, not opinions; a daily log is evidence.
quote: ensuring all entries serve as accurate, objective records

prompt: What do construction submittals help ensure?
correct: Compliance with the contract documents before the work is built
options: Compliance with the contract documents before the work is built
That the crew is paid on time
That no inspections are needed later
That drawings never need revisions
explanation: Only approved materials go into the work; submittals align the team and prevent costly mistakes.

prompt: What is the purpose of a project quality management plan?
correct: To minimize rework and avoid callbacks by doing the work right the first time
options: To minimize rework and avoid callbacks by doing the work right the first time
To set the project's selling price
To replace the safety plan
To list the crew's vacation days
explanation: The quality plan is the QA side: procedures that make the QC checks pass.
quote: create a quality management plan to minimize rework and avoid callbacks

prompt: In construction risk management, what follows risk identification?
correct: Risk quantification (probability and impact), then risk mitigation
options: Risk quantification (probability and impact), then risk mitigation
Closing the project
Ignoring low risks until they happen
Writing the as-built drawings
explanation: Identify, quantify, then mitigate: a three-step assessment.
quote: Next, master risk quantification, rating probability and impact to focus on critical challenges. Finally, develop risk mitigation strategies
